role: Regional planning organization that adopted a 6% mode split target for transit in 1990
stance_basis: SCAG adopted a 6% transit mode split target and supports guideway transit development subject to sufficient patronage and public support
summary: SCAG appears as a regional planning organization whose adopted policy goals and transportation targets are cited throughout the document. SCAG set a goal to increase transit ridership from 3.36% to 6% of all person trips by 1990, supports development of an initial guideway transit system, and provided socio-economic and land use projections used in the patronage modeling for the alternatives analysis. SCAG's stance is conditional in that it supports transit investment when justified by patronage and public support.
complaint_summary: SCAG's Draft 1978 Regional Transportation Plan is cited as the source of goals to reduce vehicle miles traveled by 5% in each five-year period from 1980 to 1995 for both air quality and fuel consumption purposes.
summary_quote: The Committee consists of representatives from SCAG, CALTRANS, The Los Angeles County Transportation Commission, the Los Angeles Community Redevelopment Agency, L. A. County and City and the SCRTD.

mentions.quote: Reduce emissions attributable to the transportation system equivalent to a reduction of vehicle miles traveled of 5% in each five-year period from 1980 to 1995. (SCAG, p. 4)
As the graph shows, the SCAG has adopted a 6% mode split target for transit in 1990 in the Regional Transportation Plan.
